newsitem.title: KENYA: Kenya set to import 639,000 tonnes of maize.
newsitem.headline: Kenya set to import 639,000 tonnes of maize.

text.p: Kenya is to import 639,000 tonnes of maize to cover a shortfall caused by a drought declared a national disaster and a production gap, food experts said on Tuesday.

"The Government of Kenya estimates that 639,000 tonnes of maize imports will be required to cover the current production shortfall," said the U.S. Agency for International Developments Famine Early Warning System (FEWS).

"The government will import 180,000 tonnes of maize, 27,000 tonnes of beans and 9,000 litres of edible oil for relief purposes. The government will also import 90,000 tonnes of maize for its strategic reserves through the National Cereals and Produce Board," FEWS said in a report.
It added the private sector would import the bulk of the maize shortfall of 369,000 tonnes and most of the 243,000 tonnes of beans required to meet food needs.

Prolonged drought in eastern and northeastern provinces of Kenya and a huge production deficit prompted President Daniel arap Moi last month to declare a national disaster and invoke emergency laws in some areas.
Moi's government also lifted a ban on maize imports and removed all duties and taxes on imported maize, pulses, milk and rice intended for relief feeding and strategic reserves.
The import duty on commercial imports of maize was also removed apparently to stimulate private sector activity.

The step was a climbdown from 1994 when Moi's government clamped taxes on food imports to promote local production and discourage dumping despite pressures from western donors to liberalise the economy.
Moi has appealed for foreign food aid to help drought victims.

FEWS said a combination of a growing structural deficit, a reduction in the area put to maize in the long rains season and a failure of the 1996/97 short rains resulted in an estimated maize deficit of 761,000 tonnes in the 1996/97 crop season.
It suggested government projections of 639,000 tonnes in maize imports was based on the availability of food substitutes such as potatoes and bananas.
Kenya's annual net production is about 2.31 million tonnes while national maize consumption is 2.65 million tonnes.
FEWS projected Kenyas population at 27 million and a consumption rate of 98 kg (216 pounds) of maize per person per year.
Last month, the U.N. World Food Programme asked donors for $12.4 million to buy 25,000 tonnes of maize, beans and vegetable oil to feed people in the east and northeast for the next six months.

Food distribution was planned for 270,000 primary school children in Eastern Province, stretching up to the Ethiopian border, and to 207,000 people in North Eastern province, which borders on Somalia.
